On the weakest agent, a retry mitigation raises success on timeout error faults from as few as 30\% of cases to 100\%, whereas stale-data faults remain near 3-4 of 10 regardless of the mitigation. AgentCheck makes these failure modes reproducible, comparable, and verifiable before deployment.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on evaluating and mitigating failure modes in agentic systems, which is a core AI safety challenge.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Embedding Orrery: Visual Exploration of Embedding Spaces and Sparse Autoencoder Features
abstract: Embedding Orrery is an open-source platform for interactive 3-dimensional visualization of embedding spaces, with native support for Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), built for data exploration and interpretability research. Given any textual, image, or vector dataset, a single pipeline - embedding, projection, clustering, automatic topic labeling and, optionally, the collection of per-document SAE feature activations - turns it into a 3D constellation that can be searched visually, semantically, lexically, or by SAE feature names; probes can be trained, configured and scored directly in the interface. SAEs are automatically downloaded and rendered as navigable constellations in which entering a prompt highlights the features it activates. Individual features can be inspected inside a dashboard and injected into the model for causal steering. The star-cartography-inspired interface sustains up to 500,000 points, including WebGL animations and volumetric nebula shaders, on 8 GB of RAM. Embedding Orrery is released under the Apache 2.0 license. Code: https://github.com/Giacomo-De-Luca/embedding-orrery. HF Spaces: https://huggingface.co/spaces/GiacomoDeLuca/orrery-demo.
filter_reasoning: The paper provides tools for interpretability and feature-level inspection of neural networks, which is central to AI safety.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: CLT-Forge: A Scalable Library for Cross-Layer Transcoders and Attribution Graphs
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to understand how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent and process information. Recent approaches based on dictionary learning and transcoders enable representing model computation in terms of sparse, interpretable features and their interactions, giving rise to feature attribution graphs. However, these graphs are often large and redundant, limiting their interpretability in practice. Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) address this issue by sharing features across layers while preserving layer-specific decoding, yielding more compact representations, but remain difficult to train and analyze at scale. We introduce an open-source library for end-to-end training and interpretability of CLTs. Our framework integrates scalable distributed training with model sharding and compressed activation caching, a unified automated interpretability pipeline for feature analysis and explanation, attribution graph computation using Circuit-Tracer, and a flexible visualization interface. This provides a practical and unified solution for scaling CLT-based mechanistic interpretability. Our code is available at https://github.com/LLM-Interp/CLT-Forge.
filter_reasoning: Mechanistic interpretability of LLMs is a core subfield of AI safety research.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: HiMe: Real-Time Self-Hosted Personal Agent Platform for Health Insights with Wearable Devices
abstract: Traditional approaches to wearable health signal analysis, such as smartwatches, are constrained by rigid analytical frameworks and limited personalisation. The emergence of LLM agents creates a new opportunity for Personal Health Agentic Analysis, where health insights can be generated adaptively and in context. However, currently there is no open-source locally deployable platform capable of processing personal health data in real time while preserving privacy. We present , a locally deployable, privacy-first agent platform that is fully compatible with real-time health data ecosystems across a wide range of wearable devices. is guided by three design principles. The database is treated as a first-class component. Effectiveness and efficiency are jointly optimised to achieve a low-cost Pareto-optimal balance. Data are processed in real time while the user is modelled over the long term. Together, these principles make it practical for individuals to harness Personal Health Agents for continuous, personalised health monitoring for better wellbeing.
filter_reasoning: The paper explicitly focuses on developing a privacy-first agent platform for sensitive personal health data, which is a core AI ethics and privacy concern.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Rethinking Content Moderation via Severity-Aware Ranking
abstract: Online video content moderation is critical for protecting minors. Violations are increasingly implicit and context-dependent: a swimwear is innocuous in a vlog but high-risk with suggestive posing. Yet, traditional binary systems fundamentally fail to capture this continuous severity spectrum, directly leading to both excessive false positives for context-heavy samples and missing deeply implicit violations. We introduce KUROKO, a content moderation system that acts as a behind-the-scenes assistant, driving a paradigm shift in content moderation from binary classification to severity-aware ranking. Our contributions are threefold: (1) Human-Centric Severity Ranking: KUROKO shifts from rigid binary divides to a continuous risk spectrum, producing nuanced, expert-level rationales closely aligning with human judgment. (2) Verifiable Alignment and Interpretability: By integrating a severity-aware data engine and a verifiable reinforcement learning approach, we replace black-box decisions with transparent, actionable diagnostics. (3) Cost-Efficient Deployment: We engineer a coarse-to-fine inference architecture equipped with a lightweight recall classifier, enabling compact models to rival proprietary VLMs at a fraction of the computational cost. Extensive offline and online A/B tests demonstrate KUROKO's advantages over traditional binary baselines and its competitiveness with leading commercial APIs at a fraction of their scale. Online, KUROKO yields more human-confirmed enforcement actions under an equal human-review budget, while lowering violative exposure and user negative feedback.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on improving content moderation by addressing the nuances of implicit risk, aiming for transparent, verifiable alignment and accountability in moderation systems.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Predefined-Tool Execution for Reliable LLM Agents in Semiconductor Lot Analysis
abstract: LLM agents for structured data analysis rely on dynamic query generation, in which the model synthesises tool calls at runtime. This introduces failures such as fabricated dataset references, unsupported operations, and incorrect results, which existing mitigations reduce but do not eliminate. We propose predefined-tool execution as an architectural alternative in which the language model selects and parameterises tools from a fixed, schema-validated registry. We formalise the approach using typed tool specifications and prove executability and hallucination-suppression properties under assumptions. We complement the architecture with a Numerical Faithfulness Checker that verifies quantitative claims against pre-computed ground truth, and evaluate the system on a domain-specific benchmark using four language-model backbones. The suppression property follows from the validation layer under those assumptions, and held across all 276 evaluated agent executions involving 23 queries, four backbones and three runs. Mean exact-plan-match rates ranged from 50.7 to 53.6 per cent, with a between-backbone spread within a single backbone. Because exact plan match penalises valid but non-minimal plans, it is a strict lower bound on task correctness. Given only three runs per backbone, comparisons are descriptive, not evidence of equivalence The on-premise open-weight backbones performed comparably to commercial ones on the measured metrics, supporting confidential deployments.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses hallucinations and reliability in agentic tool execution, proposing architectural mitigations and verifiable faithfulness checkers.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: When Not to Think: Mitigating the Overthinking Effect in Content Moderation
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has become a default paradigm across reasoning-intensive tasks and is widely assumed to be, at worst, harmless. Recent efficient-reasoning work treats unnecessary CoT purely as a cost to be reduced. We show that in boundary-dense classification tasks such as content moderation and toxicity detection, CoT is instead actively harmful. We identify the overthinking effect: extended reasoning amplifies weak surface signals into false evidence of violation, inflating false positive rates on ambiguous non-violating samples while its gains on ambiguous violating samples mask the harm in aggregate metrics. To address this, we propose Oreki, an adaptive CoT framework that uses K-fold cross-probing to label per-sample reasoning necessity and fine-tunes on a mixture of full-reasoning and reasoning-skipped formats. Across four base models on video moderation and multi-label toxicity detection, Oreki preserves CoT's recall gains while suppressing its false positive inflation, outperforming both Always-CoT and Never-CoT. On toxicity detection, it cuts low-agreement false positive rate from 0.467 to 0.257 while raising overall F1 from 0.792 to 0.851.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses the 'overthinking' effect where excessive reasoning leads to false positives in safety-critical tasks like content moderation, directly aiming at improving model reliability.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality through Agentic Rule Discovery
abstract: High-stakes tabular pipelines rely on scattered, static quality checks that are hard to evolve and audit against policy intent. Regulated domains particularly suffer as the LLM-era automation raises expectations for traceability and accountability. We propose a vision for an ontology-grounded, repository-native data quality layer in which rules are first-class artifacts: versioned, provenance-linked to governance texts, and re-playable through immutable execution traces. As a first step toward validating this vision, we present a concrete implementation of its agentic rule-discovery core with two rule acquisition modes (Full-Agentic and Guided) and a human-in-the-loop (HITL) review interface. We define an evaluation framework and run experiments addressing whether our fully autonomous, divide-and-conquer agentic rule discovery produces rules of the same quality and diversity as those specified by a human expert, reporting preliminary results on two real world industry datasets in the finance and retail domains.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on auditability, traceability, and accountability of data quality rules in regulated domains, which is a core theme in AI ethics governance.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: SAFARI: An Industrial Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for safety-critical engineering, yet their reliability in regulated functional-safety workflows remains underexplored. We introduce SAFARI (Safety-Aware Functional Automotive Risk Inference), the first industrial benchmark for LLM-assisted automotive Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA) under ISO 26262. It contains 3,000 de-identified industrial HARA cases and evaluates two coupled tasks: open-ended hazard analysis and standards-grounded risk assessment. To evaluate open-ended HARA artifacts, we propose the first reference-anchored LLM-as-a-judge protocol with high expert correlation. Experiments with nine frontier LLMs show that models often produce plausible hazard narratives but remain weak at ISO 26262 risk classification, with the best ASIL macro-F1 reaching only 0.261. Chain-of-Thought prompting provides limited benefit and often degrades categorical risk assessment. Error analysis further localizes major failures to scenario-critical context omissions during hazard generation and to controllability misjudgments during risk assessment, indicating where expert oversight should be concentrated. The dataset can be obtained from https://github.com/xixi47520-hash/HARA.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on evaluating the reliability and performance of LLMs in functional-safety workflows for the automotive industry, which falls under AI safety.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Scaling Reinforcement Learning for Content Moderation with Large Language Models
abstract: Large-scale content moderation requires models that can apply complex, evolving policies under limited expert supervision. We present an empirical study of reinforcement learning (RL) for policy-grounded moderation across three production-derived tasks. Using established RL and inference primitives, we develop three integrity-specific designs: a policy-grounded full-trace reward, rationale-marginalized Monte Carlo scoring, and policy-structured reflection. Each design addresses an observed failure mode, including reasoning-length collapse and polarized confidence estimates. Across the three tasks, RL-Only systems trained on 200--836 labeled examples remain competitive with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) systems trained on thousands of examples, corresponding to up to approximately one order of magnitude greater label efficiency at the evaluated operating points. Performance generally improves with additional data and training compute before saturating, although larger rollout counts exhibit variability. The strongest SFT\textrightarrowRL systems attain point-estimate performance comparable to policy-trained full-time employee (FTE) reviewers across the three tasks.
filter_reasoning: This research addresses the safety of content moderation policies and reliability of model behavior, which relates to AI safety and alignment.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: LivingArena: Do LLMs Know What Other LLMs Don't? Peer-Probing as Scalable Evaluation
abstract: Fixed benchmarks are costly to renew and cannot adapt their questions to model-specific failures. We ask whether LLMs can instead discover one another's weaknesses and turn those observations into an evaluation process. To study this question, we introduce LivingArena, an automated peer-probing framework in which models take turns testing one another. Using the interaction history, each questioner identifies potential weaknesses of its opponent and constructs targeted, verifiable questions to probe them. A 3,600-round tournament of ten models reveals a clear role asymmetry: strong answerers are not always reliable questioners, because they may generate internally inconsistent tests or fail to verify their own reference answers. After a questioner exposes an answerer's failure, it is more likely to pursue the same capability domain, while the answerer's weakness recurs on independently generated questions, including questions written by different models. These findings show that peer probing can reveal persistent model-specific weaknesses while separately evaluating answering and reliable test construction. By automating this process and allowing test difficulty to evolve with model capabilities, LivingArena provides a ``living'' benchmark for model development, red-teaming, and capability-aware multi-agent coordination. We publicly release our code.[<https://github.com/galaxyChen/LivingArena>]
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a framework for red-teaming and discovering model-specific weaknesses through peer-probing, which is a direct contribution to AI safety evaluation.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: When Evaluators Cry Wolf: Lessons from Production LLM-as-Judge Evaluation in Educational AI
abstract: MagicSchool's K--12 AI product suite is used by millions of teachers and serves millions of teacher and student messages each month. Our team monitors output along four priority dimensions---student safety, tone and instructional role, pedagogical value, and structural output quality---and tracks how often it fails on each. As our program matured, false positives came to dominate the evaluators' flags, misdirecting scarce analyst attention away from failures that warrant product change. To address this, we deployed three enhancements---unanimous-fail panels of repeated judge runs, per-evaluator judge-model choices, and softened rubrics---backed by a pair of synthetic datasets: a benchmark that measures how often cases are flagged, and an egregious-failure set as a check that severe cases still fail. That set is human-reviewed, with 12 to 79 cases per evaluator, each designed to exhibit an unambiguous violation of the failure mode it targets. Across 21 deployed evaluators, final configurations reached a median benchmark activation rate of 0.04\% (16 of 21 at or below 0.2\%; 8 at 0.00\%). The strategy cuts confirmed false-positive flags by 99\% and raises per-flag precision from 0.6\% to 49\%, while holding egregious-failure capture at 100\% and improving it on 8 of 21 evaluators.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses the monitoring of safety violations and failures in educational AI, specifically focusing on refining safety-related evaluators to minimize false positives and misdirection.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: How to Speculate about Uncertainty in Agentic Coding? A Draft-Model Gate Method
abstract: LLM agents deployed for software engineering fail expensively: they act confidently wrong, and bad actions are recognized only after costly execution and retry. We present Speculative Uncertainty (SU), a method that recovers a predictive failure signal for a black-box agent from its output tokens alone, with no access to logits, weights, activations, or repeated sampling. Inverting speculative decoding, a small open-weight draft model scores the agent's already-generated trajectory in a single forward pass. From these speculative cross-likelihoods we extract phase-aware features by separating the reasoning and action spans, and calibrate them against a verifiable objective. SU produces a failure-likelihood score that any downstream policy, such as routing, human intervention, or extra test-time compute, can consume directly. To show the signal is actionable, we instantiate one such policy, a pre-execution veto gate, on software-engineering agents Qwen3-Coder-480B and closed-source Claude 3.5 Sonnet, cutting execution error rate by 6-8 percentage points and token cost by 14-19\% in deployment, transferring to out-of-distribution benchmarks without retraining, and generalizing across agent models.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses the problem of agents acting 'confidently wrong' and introduces a predictive failure signal mechanism to gate harmful or incorrect agent actions, which is a core AI safety problem.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Beyond Dense Retrieval: A Structured-Semantic Approach for Conversation Analytics
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) based conversational systems generate vast interaction logs containing critical diagnostic signals such as failure modes and safety violations. However, the cross-turn dependencies, implicit state, and topic drift inherent to these conversations defeat dense retrieval, whose lone embedding cannot concurrently encode discrete structured constraints (e.g., refusal type) and open-ended semantic content. Our central claim is conceptual: conversational retrieval must span two complementary information planes, structured metadata and semantic content, and these are best reconciled by a unified hybrid representation that jointly supports filtering over structured metadata fields and vector similarity search over unbounded open-ended fields. We instantiate this as the Extract-Annotate-Query (EAQ) framework, which derives a metadata taxonomy, applies LLM-driven annotation, and compiles natural-language queries into hybrid graph operations. On the CDR-Benchmark, EAQ lifts NDCG@10 by 30.8\% over the strongest dense baseline, with consistent gains across five analytical categories and two external datasets.
filter_reasoning: The paper specifically targets the analysis of failure modes and safety violations in conversational logs, providing a framework to monitor and audit these sensitive interactions.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Predicate Importance Estimation and Decoupled Rationale-Score Distillation for Entity Alignment
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used as structured context for Large Language Models (LLMs), but industrial KG-RAG systems often need to integrate public and domain-specific KGs constructed from heterogeneous databases. This integration relies on Entity Alignment (EA), where lexical matching alone is insufficient under predicate-name variation and incomplete local neighborhoods. We address EA for KG integration by constructing a pairwise EA dataset and proposing two complementary modules: Predicate Importance Estimation (PIE) and Decoupled Rationale-Score Distillation (DRSD). PIE is a compact embedding-based approach that removes the subject information from each 1-hop triple, encodes the resulting subjectless triples, and aggregates them with learnable predicate-importance weights to build predicate-aware entity embeddings. DRSD trains a distilled small language model (SLM) with pseudo-answers produced by a teacher LLM through distinct prompts. By converting binary EA labels into text-based supervision and decoupling confidence-score estimation from label-consistent rationales, DRSD enables the SLM to learn task-specific reasoning while retaining a less label-biased confidence signal. Experiments show that PIE and DRSD improve EA classification. Moreover, because DRSD decouples confidence-score estimation from the decision, a division between the two flags an uncertain prediction for human review, thereby enabling a practical discrepancy between automatic acceptance and human-in-the-loop verification.
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a mechanism to decouple confidence scores from reasoning, enabling human-in-the-loop verification and managing uncertainty, which falls under AI safety and reliability.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Multi-View Structural Interpretability of Agentic Reasoning Traces
abstract: Agentic language models solve tasks through reasoning, tool calls, observations, and terminal answers, exposing rich process information beyond the final answer. For practitioners, knowing which process patterns lead to success or failure is essential to diagnose agent errors and build better process reward models without relying on final-answer supervision. However, existing analyses often evaluate only final outcomes or, when examining traces, flatten them into homogeneous step sequences, fragmenting each reasoning round into disconnected steps. Our key insight is that an agent's reasoning, action, and observation within a round are better treated as typed segments of a single underlying process state, rather than independent steps. We propose MULTI-VIEW-RA, a reasoning abstraction that represents each round through two complementary views: accumulated state and within-round change. Using unlabeled clustering and binary outcome labels, we apply MULTI-VIEW-RA to two practical use cases: diagnosing failures by surfacing the process states that separate correct from incorrect trajectories, and providing a transition-level correctness signal that is a candidate source of process supervision. Across Math, HotpotQA, and FEVER with multiple Qwen and Llama models, MULTI-VIEW-RA outperforms step-level explainability baselines in cases with sufficient success rates, with particularly strong gains on longer, tool-rich traces.
filter_reasoning: The paper introduces a method for interpretability of agentic reasoning traces to diagnose failures, which aligns with AI safety research.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Uncertainty Guardrails for LLM-Based Medical Diagnostic Systems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted in clinical practice, e.g., in medical diagnostic systems. However, their reliability is still a concern, as LLMs are prone to hallucinations and could lead to misdiagnosis, inappropriate treatment decisions, and potential harm to patients. To mitigate these risks, LLM-based medical diagnostic systems should incorporate safety guardrails capable of detecting suspicious predictions and flagging them for human review or further clinical assessment. In this work, we employ uncertainty quantification (UQ) as a safety mechanism within an enterprise diagnostic system. We evaluate 16 UQ methods and propose two task-specific modifications tailored to the medical diagnostic workflow. First, we show that methods based on semantic similarity between generated samples substantially benefit from replacing a general-purpose NLI model with a domain-specific model. Second, we adapt a supervised UQ method that relies on LLM internal states for the detection of erroneous generation from a black-box enterprise LLM accessible only through a text-generation API. Our approach leverages the internal states of an open-source, lightweight proxy white-box model. We demonstrate that this approach outperforms all other UQ methods in the considered setting.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses safety, reliability, and hallucination in medical diagnostic systems through uncertainty quantification guardrails.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Audio Front-End Decoupling: Why Synthetic-Voice Simulators Fail to Predict Real-World Voice Agent Behavior
abstract: LLM-based voice agents are routinely cleared for deployment using synthetic audio regression suites, with engineering teams treating augmented commercial TTS as a safe proxy for real human callers. This paper presents the first systematic approach to quantify the profound behavioral drift that occurs when agents optimized on simulated audio are deployed in the real world. We demonstrate that the assumption of acoustic equivalence fundamentally fails: real production audio triggers 2-13 times more VAD misfires than synthetic data across Silero, WebRTC, and TEN-VAD, while simulated environments cause text-grounded turn detectors to artificially flip decisions 33\% of the time, compared to just 3\% in reality. A paired four-vendor TTS calibration sweep proves this misranking is structural: on every front-end component, optimizing thresholds for synthetic audio actively degrades real-world performance. To prevent teams from flying blind, we introduce a novel set of signal-layer metrics and an open-source framework to audit any simulator prior to adoption. Rather than testing the agent, our method tests the simulator against real target-domain interactions. By identifying where a simulator's acoustics deviate from reality, teams can definitively know which front-end tuning decisions are safe to trust.
filter_reasoning: The paper investigates the failure of synthetic data as a safety proxy for real-world agent behavior and provides a framework to audit simulators, directly relevant to AI safety testing.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Deploying LLM Agents for Auditable Complaint Investigation in Banking
abstract: Complaint investigation in retail banking requires handlers to synthesise evidence from heterogeneous enterprise systems into policy-aligned summaries. We present a production-deployed tool-augmented LLM agent at a major UK retail bank that assists this process under human review. Given a complaint record, the agent queries 16 typed, schema-validated tools and returns an investigation summary with a source-cited chronological evidence timeline. We evaluate the system using SME assessment, LLM-as-a-Judge monitoring, rework measurement, and downstream impact testing. On 187 paired complaints, SMEs judged the agent to match or exceed historical human-written production investigations in 90\% of cases across faithfulness, relevance, completeness, and coherence. Median investigation time falls from 30 minutes to 23 seconds. Operational controls include daily automated monitoring, pre-defined thresholds, hallucination flagging, and periodic human audit. These results demonstrate that constrained single-agent LLMs with typed tools are viable for scalable, auditable complaint investigation in regulated environments.
filter_reasoning: The paper discusses deploying agents for auditable and accountable processes in a regulated environment, highlighting operational controls and human oversight.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science
abstract: Evaluating LLM-powered AutoML agents for enterprise data science requires more than final leaderboard scores: agents must deliver reproducible, leakage-free, protocol-valid workflows on organization-specific data before deployment. We introduce GRACE-DS, a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science for evaluating tabular machine learning agents in real-world-like conditions. GRACE-DS stages the full workflow---planning, data inspection, feature engineering, modeling, validation, code repair, and final submission---inside an isolated sandbox where evaluator-owned labels and hidden tests remain private. Hidden executable validators track both predictive progress and process reliability, including leakage avoidance, reproducibility, validation discipline, correction behavior, reward alignment, and terminal submission validity. Based on 7,000 episodes spanning 8 LLMs, 10 tasks, 15 regimes, ablations, reward-optimization probes, and red-team settings, the structured flexible iterative regime (our approach) achieves the strongest end-to-end normalized hidden-test quality, outperforming single shot, unstructured agent, and restart baselines while improving protocol-valid completion. These results establish GRACE-DS as a controlled pre-deployment harness for diagnosing whether LLM-powered AutoML agents satisfy core enterprise execution constraints, on a deliberately search-free tabular sub-problem that isolates planning, correction, and validation discipline from expensive model search. An earlier version of this paper is available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16000v2; code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/Alexx221x/GRACE-DS/tree/archive.
filter_reasoning: The paper provides a harness for evaluating agent reliability, protocol validity, and reward alignment in enterprise settings.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Calibrated Deferral Routing for Cost-Efficient Guardrails
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance across diverse NLP tasks, but deploying them in real-world scenarios raises concerns regarding safety, reliability, and computational cost. To mitigate the risk of harmful, unreliable, or unfaithful content, LLM pipelines increasingly rely on guardrails. Yet deploying multiple guardrails across different tasks and risk categories introduces significant computational and orchestration overhead. In this work, we propose a calibrated deferral-routing framework for deploying guardrails both accurately and cost-effectively. Our approach arranges guardrails as a cascade of increasing capability and cost: each input is first evaluated by a lightweight guardrail, while only uncertain instances are deferred to a larger, more capable, and more expensive model. We formalize this routing problem and study practical deferral-calibration strategies by applying post-hoc calibration, including isotonic regression, Platt scaling, and temperature scaling. We evaluate 18 guardrail models from four model families (i.e., Granite Guardian, Llama Guard, ShieldGemma, and GuardReasoner) across 10 harm-detection benchmarks. Our experiments show that: (i) all guardrail models are often poorly calibrated out of the box (ECE ranging from 6\% to 28\%); (ii) post-hoc calibration substantially improves reliability reducing ECE below 2.5\% in most cases; (iii) cascade routing yields large cost savings with minimal accuracy loss, while monotone calibration primarily makes routing thresholds deployable rather than improving rank ordering.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on cost-efficient safety guardrails, reliability, and mitigating risks of harmful/unreliable content.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: MotiGAN: Game Theory Meets the Motivated Intruder Test for Re-identification Risk Generation and Annotation in Pseudonymisation
abstract: Re-identification methods serve as a concrete instantiation of the Motivated Intruder Test in privacy-preserving problems, and current state-of-the-art attack techniques are predominantly built upon Large Language Models (LLMs) which are also core components of robust pseudonymized methods. Therefore, it requires the rich training dataset. However, as research demands continue to grow while publicly available data for each domain remains limited and the cost of direct human supervision is high, a central question arises: how can a human-in-the-loop approach be integrated to generate high-quality data and improve the performance of LLMs in psedonymization. To address this limitation, we propose MOTIGAN1 - a gamified framework that transforms the motivated intruder test into a competitive three population tournament. In this game, human characters and AI characters compete to re-identify individuals from each essay. At every stage, players both commit their guesses and contribute to enriching the synthesized dataset. In our experiments, the synthesized dataset contributes to improving the performance of multiple models in several experiments (achieving up to 37.6\% improvement on a well-established benchmark).
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses privacy-preserving pseudonymization and re-identification risk, which are central topics in AI ethics.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Catching AI-Generated Code at Scale: A Lightweight and Interpretable Detector for the LLM Era
abstract: As LLMs become everyday creative partners in software development, code is no longer a purely human artefact; it emerges from an increasingly hybrid human-AI process. Understanding who contributed which parts of a codebase has become a foundational question of creative attribution, touching on authorship, trust, and the integrity of co-created work. Yet existing detectors exceed 100M$+$ parameters, are too slow for practical deployment, and offer no insight into what distinguishes human from AI creative contributions. We present NanoDroid, a backbone-free detector with only 5.1M parameters that runs $20\times$ faster than 125M-parameter UniXcoder (SOTA) and is fully interpretable: per-stream attribution scores explicitly expose which stylistic evidence (token statistics, transition patterns, surface style) distinguishes human from AI authorship in code. On the challenging 4-class DroidCollection benchmark (Human / Machine / Refined / Adversarial), NanoDroid achieves 90.77\% weighted F1, within 2.6\% of SOTA, on the CodeT-M4 benchmark, NanoDroid achieves SOTA performance, while providing the kind of transparent decision decomposition that black-box models cannot. Beyond a detection tool, we argue NanoDroid offers a lens for studying how human and AI creativity differ stylistically, and where they blur.
filter_reasoning: The paper deals with the attribution and transparency of AI-generated content in software, touching on trust and authorship integrity.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Trace-GRAF: Trace-Guided Granularity Routing for Sequential Agentic Workflows
abstract: Multi-agent LLM results can conflate decomposition with roles, communication, parallelism, and extra compute. We study strictly ordered tool-use workflows of dependent state-changing steps, where segmentation may also support auditing and handoff constraints. We introduce Trace-GRAF, a granularity selector that aligns one single-agent trace to target workflow steps, converts order violations and unrelated drift into split pressure, and selects the smallest granularity on the minimum-pressure plateau. It executes balanced contiguous segments because boundary ablation finds no significant success difference from semantic segmentation; pressure-minimizing partitions characterize cuts. Across held-out cohorts spanning two benchmarks and three executors, fixed decomposition sometimes improves and sometimes reduces success, while greater granularity both rescues failures and regresses solved runs. When SA success is observable, the pressure route preserves successful runs by construction. Across validation resplits on TerminalWorld, the calibrated extension's mean recovery is 2.3--3.0\% for GPT-OSS, 0.0--0.1\% for Gemini, and 2.3--4.9\% for DeepSeek. Simple fixed fallbacks match much of the observed gain. Trace-GRAF therefore provides a risk-aware routing diagnostic with benchmark- and split-dependent gains.
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a diagnostic routing method to manage agentic failure modes and auditing workflows, which relates to AI safety and reliability.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: RAW: Refusal Aversion in the Wild, A Causal Measurement Method for Deployed LLMs
abstract: Deployed LLMs field hundreds of millions of conversations a day and refuse a non-trivial fraction of user requests, yet the user-side cost of refusal, whether users disengage and by how much, is unmeasured on any production model: a blind spot for the consumer-facing platforms built on them. A/B-testing refusal is ethically and operationally constrained on frontier-lab products and unavailable to third-party platforms deploying these models through a fixed API. We introduce RAW, a method that uses LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment: at near-identical prompts in any existing log, the same model sometimes refuses and sometimes does not, and that variation identifies the causal user-side effect of refusal. Applying the method to 15 deployed LLMs in LMSYS-Chat-1M and WildChat, with user-clustered inference, we find that for about half of the models we can measure precisely, a refusal costs 3 to 17 pp of subsequent re-engagement; the rest show no distinguishable effect, among them one deployment whose positive point estimate we trace to persistent users retrying the refused request. Our contribution is the measurement method, which runs on any deployed model from logs alone for about $0.30 per 1,000 conversations. We release labels, moderation scores, prompt embeddings, and pipeline code.$
filter_reasoning: The paper measures user outcomes related to model refusals, which is an important metric for evaluating AI behavior, user impact, and safety-alignment trade-offs.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Debate-to-Skill: Capability-Bound Process Supervision for Industrial Query-to-Agent Annotation
abstract: Industrial query-to-agent matching fails when topical relevance is mistaken for executable capability, especially on long-tail and boundary-sensitive requests. We formulate annotation as capability-bound process supervision and instantiate it with Debate-to-Skill, which uses reusable decision principles, structured deliberation, verifier-based verdict extraction, and disagreement-driven refinement. On an industrial Query2Agent benchmark, we compare Debate-to-Skill with direct-label supervision, reasoning-SFT, and structural ablations. The results test whether gains come from supervising the capability-critical decision process itself, especially on grey-zone cases where semantic relatedness and executable capability diverge.
filter_reasoning: The paper discusses process supervision to distinguish between semantic relevance and actual executable capability, which is a safety concern regarding model alignment.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: EvidenT: Building Trustworthy Enterprise Assistants through Evidence Groundedness and Traceability
abstract: Enterprise AI assistants must produce responses that are verifiable and traceable to source evidence. However, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over heterogeneous enterprise data can suffer from citation drift, unsupported content, and weak source traceability. We present EvidenT (T = Trust + Transparency + Traceability), a lightweight pipeline that verifies extracted evidence against retrieved documents before answer generation, without model retraining. EvidenT combines structured passage extraction with deterministic lexical alignment to filter unsupported content, correct citation drift, and preserve source-span traceability. On approximately 500 real enterprise queries, EvidenT improves gold-source hit rate by an average of 29\% over prompting baselines, produces no citations to non-retrieved urls, and achieves near-saturated answer-to-source lexical coverage.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on grounding AI responses in evidence and ensuring traceability, which falls under the interpretability/trustworthiness aspects of AI safety.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: RainbowPlus: Enhancing Adversarial Prompt Generation via Evolutionary Quality-Diversity Search
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that exploit safety mechanisms. Existing red-teaming methods face scalability challenges, computational bottlenecks, or limited attack diversity. We propose , a framework that reconceptualizes adversarial prompt generation as evolutionary quality-diversity search, where diverse attack strategies co-evolve across behavioral niches. introduces two synergistic innovations: (1) multi-element archives that maintain populations of elite solutions per niche, and (2) parallel fitness evaluation that replaces pairwise comparisons with efficient probabilistic scoring, achieving $\Theta(M)$ speedup (from $\Theta(M^2N)$ to $\Theta(MN)$). Experiments demonstrate superior performance: compared to Rainbow Teaming, generates $100\times$ more prompts (10,418 vs. 100) with higher attack success rates. Against nine state-of-the-art methods on HarmBench with 12 LLMs, achieves 81.1\% average ASR - surpassing AutoDAN-Turbo by 3.9 points - while being $9\times$ faster (1.45 vs. 13.50 hours). Code: https://github.com/knoveleng/rainbowplus
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a new method for generating adversarial prompts to test LLM robustness and safety mechanisms, clearly falling under AI safety.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Safe and Sufficient Caching: Validated Evidence Reuse for Production Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Production Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems serve repeated queries over evolving document corpora under user-specific access constraints. Standard pipelines perform full retrieval and generation for every request, wasting computation on recurring queries. Naive caching reduces latency but introduces safety failures: stale evidence from updated documents, unauthorized content crossing access boundaries, and superseded passages no longer reflecting source truth. These violations are invisible on academic benchmarks yet unacceptable in enterprise deployment. We introduce SSC (Safe and Sufficient Caching), a validated evidence reuse framework for production RAG. SSC caches evidence chunks (not generated answers) with perchunk provenance metadata, and enforces hard validity constraints before reuse: access-control gating ensures user authorization, and freshness verification confirms source-document currency. Only evidence passing both checks enters a utility-based ranking stage balancing relevance, source trust, historical utility, and serving cost. This separation of safety from efficiency is the central contribution. On WebQuestions and HotpotQA, SSC maintains full quality parity with unrestricted retrieval baselines, confirming zero degradation from evidence reuse. On a proprietary InternalQA workload with role based access control and document versioning, it reduces end-to-end latency by 22\% and retrieval cost by 34\% while achieving zero invalid reuse, compared to 3.4-9.8\% violation rates for standard caching and 0.3-8.2\% for TTL-based invalidation. The method is training-free, retriever-agnostic, and deploys as a thin validation layer in existing RAG pipelines.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses safety failures in RAG systems (stale/unauthorized content) and proposes a validated evidence reuse framework to ensure system robustness, which is a core AI safety concern.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Cognitive Echoes: Deployable Conversational Risk Screening in Automotive Finance on Constrained LLMs
abstract: Automotive-finance screening can fail when individually valid documents are paired with an internally inconsistent applicant narrative. We present the Adversarial Cognitive Probing Framework (ACPF), a theory-motivated staged protocol that scores four ordinal behavioral dimensions and delegates the final decision to a deterministic backend predicate. We evaluate ACPF on a risk-enriched retrospective corpus of 340 officer--applicant dialogues: 72 institutional adjudications of suspected misrepresentation, 138 cases of significant early delinquency, 110 good cases, and 20 non-fraud rejections excluded from the primary metrics. On identical fixed transcripts and the same QWEN3.5-122B carrier, structured scoring raises combined-risk capture from 5.7\% to 61.0\% while reducing the false-rejection rate from 14.5\% to 12.7\%. With OmniMAX, the selected low-FPR carrier, ACPF captures 58/138 (42.0\%) delinquency cases at 6/110 (5.5\%) false rejections; current origination review flags none of these delinquency cases. On the institutionally adjudicated stratum, ACPF captures 56/72 (77.8\%) versus 72/72 for current review, but we make no comparative claim because the label and reference decision share institutional provenance. A shadow deployment has no adverse-action authority; prospective outcome validation is not yet available.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses the safety of AI-assisted financial screening by building a framework to capture misrepresentation and risk, focusing on system reliability and integrity.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Open Rubric System: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Adaptive Rubric
abstract: We argue that robust alignment for non-verifiable tasks is fundamentally a $principle generalization$ problem: reward should be guided by explicit, auditable principles rather than compressed into a learned scalar function. To operationalize this view, we present the $Open Rubric System (OpenRS)$ , a modular, rubrics-based $LLM-as-a-Judge$ framework built around $Pairwise Adaptive Meta-Rubrics (PAMR)$ and lightweight $Pointwise Verifiable Rubrics$ (PVRs). OpenRS is governed by an explicit $meta-rubric$---not a rubric itself, but a higher-level guideline that specifies $how$ rubrics should be generated, which criteria to prioritize, and which failure modes are non-negotiable---and instantiates concrete $adaptive rubrics$ on the fly by conditioning on the semantic differences between two candidate responses. It then performs criterion-wise $pairwise$ comparisons and aggregates criterion-level preferences externally, avoiding pointwise weighted scalarization while improving discriminability in open-ended settings. Finally, we instantiate OpenRS as reward supervision in pairwise RL training. Empirically, OpenRS achieves state-of-the-art results on four reward-modeling benchmarks and yields stable gains when replacing scalar reward models in end-to-end RL.
filter_reasoning: The paper focuses on 'alignment' and using verifiable rubrics to guide AI behavior, which is a core concern in AI safety alignment research.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: AgentLens: Trajectory Reviews for Coding Agent Evaluation
abstract: We present AgentLens, a trajectory-level evaluation framework for interactive code agents, built from production-informed tasks and integrated into continuous regression testing. Most code-agent benchmarks reduce a run to a single bit---did the task pass?---but the people who actually use these agents experience the entire trajectory: how the agent follows instructions, uses its tools, verifies its own work, recovers from mistakes, and talks to them along the way. AgentLens evaluates that whole trajectory, pairing formal verification with LLM-written trajectory reviews and side-by-side comparisons, so that each run yields a readable explanation of the final score. Apart from ranking models, AgentLens can be used to diagnose model behavior, compare successive versions of agents, and catch product regressions in an evaluation pipeline. We release AgentLens at https://github.com/agent-lens/agent-lens-bench.
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a framework for evaluating the trajectory and behavior of code agents, which is essential for the interpretability and reliability of autonomous agents.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: CASTLE: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Student-Tailored Personalized Safety in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have advanced the development of personalized learning in education. However, their inherent generation mechanisms often produce homogeneous responses to identical prompts. This ``one-size-fits-all'' mechanism overlooks the substantial heterogeneity in students' cognitive and psychological characteristics, thereby posing potential safety risks to vulnerable groups. Existing safety evaluations primarily rely on context-independent metrics such as factual accuracy, bias, or toxicity, which fail to capture the divergent harms that the same response might cause across different student attributes. To address this gap, we propose the concept of ``Student-Tailored Personalized Safety'' and construct CASTLE based on educational theories. This benchmark covers 15 educational safety risks and 14 student attributes, comprising 92,908 bilingual scenarios. We further design three evaluation metrics: Risk Sensitivity, measuring the model's ability to detect risks; Emotional Empathy, evaluating the model's capacity to recognize student states; and Student Alignment, assessing the match between model responses and student attributes. Experiments on 18 LLMs demonstrate that CASTLE poses a significant challenge: all models scored below an average safety score of 2.5 out of 5, indicating substantial deficiencies in personalized safety assurance. The code is available at https://github.com/ECNU-RAIL/CASTLE-EMNLP2026.
filter_reasoning: The paper explicitly addresses 'Student-Tailored Personalized Safety' and evaluates risks regarding bias and fairness in an educational context.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: EgoArgus: Benchmarking VLMs as Situational Assistants for Modality-Grounded User Supports
abstract: VLMs are increasingly positioned as daily assistants that perceive first-person environments, follow user dialogue, and decide how to help. Existing egocentric benchmarks mainly evaluate visual understanding in isolation, leaving open whether models can arbitrate between visual evidence and user-provided language when the two are helpful, irrelevant, or conflicting. We introduce EgoArgus, a human-annotated dataset for evaluating egocentric assistants on understanding and decision tasks in five dialogue-video daily scenarios. Our results demonstrate that it is still challenging for current VLMs as reliable egocentric assistants, which requires identifying which modality is trustworthy and deciding when intervention is warranted. Deeper analysis also shows that existing modality bias mitigation methods are quite restricted to enhance performance, providing insights to aid practioners into the deployment of current VLMs as daily assistants.
filter_reasoning: The paper evaluates the reliability and modality-trustworthiness of VLM assistants, which directly relates to the safety and robustness of AI agents.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Beneath the Diff: Diagnosing and Mitigating Algorithmic Mode Collapse in Code-Level Autonomous Research Loops
abstract: Code-level autonomous research loops (ARLs) have recently emerged as a concrete object of study in automated machine learning research. In such loops, an LLM agent proposes modifications to an experimental training pipeline, executes the modified pipeline, and retains edits that improve a verifiable in-loop metric. Although executable metrics may appear to provide a reliable signal of progress, it remains unclear whether repeated metric-driven code editing leads to genuine improvements that generalize beyond the loop. We provide a systematic diagnosis of this question. Across various experiment settings, we identify a robust failure mode that we call **algorithmic mode collapse**. In this regime, surface-level edit diversity remains stable, but semantic and mechanism-level diversity collapse: the agent continues to edit different lines of code while repeatedly proposing the same kinds of algorithmic changes. This collapse is accompanied by a widening gap between in-loop metric gains and gains measured on independent held-out evaluations. We then propose Diversity-Aware Proposal Sampling (DAPS), a lightweight mitigation that combines category-coverage reweighting, persistent edit memory, and a validation gate. Under a three-tier protocol separating the in-loop metric, the audit metric read by the gate, and a blind metric no loop component ever accesses, DAPS reduces semantic-cluster decay of edits by $69.1%$ and improves relative faithfulness by $83.7%$ blind and $81.6%$ audited, while preserving in-loop optimization speed. We provide the code in Github [repository](https://github.com/BokwaiHo/arl-mode-collapse).$
filter_reasoning: The paper diagnoses 'algorithmic mode collapse' in autonomous agents, which relates to the safety, reliability, and robustness of autonomous research agents.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Same Chart, Different Story: Bias in Vision-Language Chart Interpretation
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used to interpret charts and generate natural-language explanations for socially consequential data. However, they may produce different narratives for the same chart when only the referenced social group changes, reinforcing stereotypes and misleading decisions. Despite these risks, no benchmark exists for systematically evaluating bias in chart interpretation across social dimensions. We introduce ChartBias, the first benchmark for auditing bias in VLM-based chart interpretation. ChartBias contains 820 manually curated real-world charts spanning six attributes---race, income, age, religion, immigration status, and gender---yielding 4,319 valid chart--attribute instances and 8,638 paired generations where the chart is fixed and only the group term is swapped. Across 12 proprietary and open-source VLMs, totaling 155,484 model responses, we find three widespread failure modes: narrative shift (same chart, different narratives), group hallucination (assigning a chart to a group without evidence), and preference polarity (favourable trends often linked to one group). We further propose a multi-agent mitigation framework that serves as a strong baseline by separating chart-grounded evidence extraction from group-conditioned generation and using a counterfactual judge to verify that group-driven differences are supported by the chart. The framework substantially reduces narrative shift while preserving chart-grounded reasoning. Our findings show that evaluating chart understanding requires measuring not only accuracy, but also fairness and consistency across social groups. We release ChartBias at <redacted>.
filter_reasoning: The paper investigates and mitigates stereotypical biases in vision-language chart interpretation across social groups.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: When Counterfactual Debiasing Backfires: Identity Cues as Task-Dependent Evidence in Harmful Language Understanding
abstract: Counterfactual debiasing is often used to reduce reliance on identity-linked shortcuts in harmful language understanding. We show that the same intervention can be harmful when identity mentions are not shortcuts but label-defining evidence. In multi-task cyberbullying modeling, identity cues may be spurious for cyberbullying detection (CD) and sentiment analysis (SA), yet necessary for fine-grained target identification (TI). We propose task-aware routing, which sends CD and SA through a debiased representation while preserving the original representation for TI. We evaluate this approach on the English-translated BullyExplain benchmark, HateXplain, and an external Measuring Hate Speech diagnostic. Experiments show that task-aware routing improves TI, while auxiliary detection and sentiment performance remain largely unchanged where applicable. Ablation studies attribute this improvement to representation routing that preserves identity-bearing evidence for TI rather than to class-weighting choices, with reduced-architecture diagnostics suggesting that the effect is not specific to the graph-enhanced model. These results support a task-conditional view of counterfactual debiasing: the same identity cue can warrant suppression in one task and preservation in another.
filter_reasoning: The paper examines the intersection of identity-based debiasing and task-dependent model fairness in harmful language detection.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: How Stable Is In-Context Learning? Lipschitz Bounds for Transformer Output under Context Perturbation
abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables large language models to adapt from a few demonstrations, yet its sensitivity to context perturbations remains poorly understood. We study the context-conditioned map $ C \mapsto f_\theta(x; C) $ through Lipschitz analysis. Modeling the Transformer as a composition of attention and feed-forward layers, we derive a worst-case certificate $ |f(x; C + \delta) - f(x; C)| \leq L|\delta| $ and a data-dependent local estimator based on finite-difference Jacobian probes. Across six language models (117M--7B) on controlled arithmetic ICL tasks, we find that: (i) output changes saturate as perturbation magnitude increases; (ii) global spectral bounds are extremely conservative, while local estimates are far closer to empirical sensitivity; (iii) sensitivity concentrates in late attention layers; (iv) additional demonstrations often stabilize predictions through redundancy; and (v) perturbation direction matters: label flips have much larger normalized effect than reorderings. SST-2 validation supports the same local-sensitivity and perturbation-direction trends. Our results position Lipschitz analysis less as a tight global predictor and more as a diagnostic framework for locating and comparing ICL vulnerabilities.
filter_reasoning: The paper uses Lipschitz analysis to certify the robustness and sensitivity of in-context learning, which falls under AI model robustness.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Authority Bias in Conversational Search Engines for Academic Paper Recommendation.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as conversational search engines for academic literature, yet whether they judge papers on content or on authority signals has not been tested causally. We investigate authority bias: systematic preference for papers based on author prestige, venue, and citations rather than content. Holding title and abstract constant, we vary authority metadata across three counterfactual conditions (original, flipped, boosted) over eight LLMs (five open-weight and three frontier closed-weight) in an in-context, single-turn, top-1 recommendation setting. Our experiments show that authority bias is substantial and directional, varies markedly across models, and is only partially addressable through prompt-level debiasing. We further document a say-do gap: debiasing instructions suppress authority mentions far faster than authority-driven flips, so surface auditing systematically underestimates behavioral bias.\par Code: https://github.com/jinaduuthman/Authority-Bias-In-Conversational-Search-Engine\par Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/uthmanjinadu/authority-bias-paper-recommendation
filter_reasoning: The paper investigates systemic authority bias in AI models, a key concern in AI ethics regarding fairness and algorithmic representation.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety--Utility Balancing
abstract: LLM-based agents can interact with external environments through tool invocation, but this capability also introduces security risks such as file modification, information leakage, and unauthorized actions. Existing guardrails often evaluate completed trajectories, leaving pre-execution monitoring of step-level actions underexplored. We propose StepGuard, a step-level guard model that can audit completed agent trajectories and check tool actions before they are executed. To train StepGuard, we introduce StepGen, an automatic data engine that generates safe and unsafe trajectories with the same context but different actions at the risky step. To further reduce over-defense and under-defense, we propose Balance-GRPO, which dynamically balances learning between safe and unsafe actions based on their observed accuracy. Experiments show that StepGuard achieves the highest average accuracy among open-weight guard models, with performance comparable to GPT-5.4. When used to guard agents on AgentDojo and AgentDyn, StepGuard reduces mean ASR by 77.3\% relative to the no-guard setting, while mean utility drops by only 2.8 points.
filter_reasoning: The paper develops guardrails to prevent harmful agent actions, falling directly into AI safety's focus on robustness and controlling agent behavior.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: UNISAF-Bench: Intention-Grounded Safety Evaluation for Unified Multimodal Generation Models
abstract: Unified Multi-Modal Generation (UMMG) models support seamless switching between generation tasks spanning multiple modality combinations within a single conversational interface. However, existing safety benchmarks construct prompts independently per modality, so different modalities cover different harmful intentions, preventing holistic evaluation of UMMG models. We propose an intention-grounded evaluation methodology in which every modality combination is evaluated against the same set of harmful intentions, yielding fair, directly comparable safety scores across modalities. Because scores are aggregated at the intention level --- averaging over the same set of intentions rather than over modality-specific prompt sets --- each model receives an accurate safety profile not distorted by per-modality differences. The methodology is incrementally extensible: new modality combinations or intentions can be added without rebuilding existing data. Following this methodology, we construct UNISAF-Bench (UNIfied intention-grounded SAFety Benchmark): 1,257 human-verified harmful intentions across 19 policies, yielding 20,112 conversations spanning 4 modality combinations, single-/multi-turn settings, and paired policy-violating/boundary-benign variants. Evaluation of four open-source UMMG models reveals systematic safety gaps: multimodal inputs degrade text-output safety, safety alignment fails to transfer to image generation, and multi-turn deflection bias inflates refusal on both harmful and benign prompts.
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes a new benchmark to evaluate safety alignment across multiple modalities in unified models.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data
abstract: LLMs over external data face a per-instruction tension: a single document or tool return often interleaves legitimate directives with adversarial prompt injections, and the model must follow the former while rejecting the latter. Existing defenses suppress or trust all external instructions, collapsing the safety-utility frontier and forcing a choice between over-refusal and over-compliance. We argue the missing capability is **per-instruction credit attribution** and formalize it as External-Data Instruction Classification, an identify-classify-act decision over each embedded directive. We propose **EDIC**, a decomposed reward framework for per-instruction compliance. A scene-grounded pipeline injects mixed beneficial and harmful instructions with counterfactual filtering, while a generative judge is initialized by SFT and refined with GRPO to attribute compliance at the instruction level. The judge then produces a reward that separately encourages beneficial compliance and penalizes harmful compliance for RL training. Across two backbones and five benchmarks, EDIC improves both safety and utility over the strongest prior defense, lifting harmful-rejection by up to 7.7\% and Arena-Hard-Auto utility by 12.5\% on Qwen3-4B.
filter_reasoning: The paper introduces a framework to distinguish between beneficial and harmful instructions, addressing the safety challenge of prompt injection and model alignment.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: HARVE: Hacking-Aware Reward-Head Vector Editing for Robust Reward Models
abstract: Reward models are central to large language model (LLM) alignment, but they remain vulnerable to reward hacking. To evaluate reward-model robustness, we introduce RewardHackBench containing 13 reward-hacking patterns covering real life high-stakes domains and general settings, and we find severe failures on specific subcategories across eight reward models. To mitigate these failures, we propose HARVE, a training-free reward-head editing method for scalar reward models. Instead of fine-tuning the reward model, HARVE identifies a multi-directional hacking subspace from residual-stream directions associated with selected hacking subcategories, and removes the component of the reward-head vector aligned with that subspace. This directly reduces the reward head's sensitivity to hacking-related features using only a small set of contrastive gold-hacked examples, without gradient updates or fine-tuning. Comprehensive experiments across eight reward models indicates that improves hacking robustness, outperforms fine-tuning baselines, and preserves reward-models' general capability. Further analyses show that combining multiple target-specific residual-stream directions is more effective than relying on a single surface-level feature.
filter_reasoning: The paper addresses reward hacking, a core AI safety challenge, by proposing a training-free method to increase reward model robustness.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Is my model perplexed for the right reason? Contrasting LLMs' Benchmark Behavior with Token-Level Perplexity
abstract: Standard evaluations of Large language models (LLMs) focus on task performance, offering limited insight into whether correct behavior reflects appropriate underlying mechanisms and risking confirmation bias. We introduce a simple, principled interpretability framework based on token-level perplexity to test whether models rely on linguistically relevant cues. By comparing perplexity distributions over minimal sentence pairs differing in one or a few `pivotal' tokens, our method enables precise, hypothesis-driven analysis without relying on unstable feature-attribution techniques. Experiments on controlled linguistic benchmarks with several open-weight LLMs show that, while linguistically important tokens influence model behavior, they never fully explain perplexity shifts, revealing that models rely on heuristics other than the expected linguistic ones.
filter_reasoning: The paper uses interpretability techniques (token-level perplexity) to examine whether models are relying on appropriate linguistic cues, which falls under explainability.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Prompt injection is listed as the \#1 threat to AI agents. When an agent accesses external data from websites, files, or emails, an attacker may inject a prompt into the data, saying, ``Ignore all prior instructions and perform <an attacker's task>.'' To prevent arbitrary manipulation of agents, defenders try to train secure LLMs, which, however, still suffer from near 100\% attack success rates (ASRs) against adaptive prompt injections. We note that this is because existing defensive fine-tuning recipes rely on sequence-level feedback signals (in DPO or GRPO). Treating an entire output equally prevents the model from learning precisely which output tokens are insecure. In this paper, we propose Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD) that provides token-level feedback to guide defensive fine-tuning. The LLM receives an injected sample and produces a rollout, whose tokens are scored by the initialization model given the corresponding clean input. With more fine-grained training signals, our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0\% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0\% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign. The obtained security generalizes to domains completely unseen in training: in agentic tool calling, SecOPD achieves a 4.7\% ASR compared to 5.5\% for Meta-SecAlign.
filter_reasoning: The paper directly addresses the AI safety challenge of preventing adversarial prompt injection in agents.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Man Made Language Models? Evaluating LLMs' Perpetuation of Masculine Generics Bias
abstract: Instruct-based large language models (LLMs) have been shown to propagate and even amplify gender bias when prompted with contextually constrained instructions (e.g., writing a text from a description or selecting a gendered pronoun). However, little attention has been paid to biases in responses to contextually unconstrained (generic) instructions conveyed by gendered language, particularly masculine generics (MG). MG, found in many gender-marked languages, denote the use of the masculine gender as a supposedly ``neutral'' reference for mixed-gender groups or for individuals of unknown gender. Yet, psycholinguistic studies demonstrate that MG are not neutral and systematically induce gender bias. This study investigates how both local and proprietary LLMs are MG-biased when responding to generic prompts in French, examining LLMs' MG bias rates and use of gender-fair language (GFL). We create a 16k+ human noun database from existing lexical resources and evaluate six LLMs on four instruction-response datasets under two conditions: prompts with and without MG. Overall, we find that \approx27.57\% of LLMs' responses to MG-filtered generic instructions are MG-biased (\approx78.55\% with MG-containing prompts). Moreover, we find that LLMs rarely use GFL spontaneously. These findings highlight the persistence of MG bias in LLM outputs and the models' limited tendency towards GFL strategies.
filter_reasoning: The paper directly investigates and measures social bias (specifically gender bias/masculine generics) in LLMs.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: The Straight and Narrow: Do LLMs Possess an Internal Moral Path?
abstract: Enhancing the moral alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is a critical challenge, yet current techniques like RLHF often function as superficial behavioral guardrails, leaving the model's internal moral representations untouched and susceptible to complex jailbreaks. In this paper, we propose a shift from behavioral intervention to latent space steering by leveraging Moral Foundations Theory (MFT). To ensure these internal representations capture moral concepts shared across different languages rather than superficial linguistic patterns, we first conduct a cross-lingual linear probing analysis, validating a shared yet culturally nuanced moral subspace between Chinese and English. Establishing this robust semantic foundation allows us to extract steerable Moral Vectors with high causal efficacy at both internal and behavioral levels. Finally, we introduce Adaptive Moral Fusion (AMF), a dynamic inference-time intervention that balances the safety-helpfulness trade-off. Empirical results demonstrate that AMF serves as a targeted intrinsic defense, significantly reducing jailbreak success rates on HarmBench while minimizing incorrect refusals on XSTest compared to standard baselines.
filter_reasoning: The paper proposes methods to steer internal moral representations for improved safety and reduced jailbreak susceptibility.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: What Drives Paper Acceptance? A Process-Centric Analysis of Modern Peer Review
abstract: Peer review is the primary mechanism for evaluating scientific contributions, yet prior studies have mostly examined paper features or external metadata in isolation. The emergence of open platforms such as OpenReview has transformed peer review into a transparent and interactive process, recording not only scores and comments but also rebuttals, reviewer--author exchanges, and meta-reviewer decisions. In this paper, we present a large-scale empirical study of ICLR 2017--2025, encompassing over 28,000 submissions, integrating four dimensions: paper structure and language quality, submission strategies and external metadata, author--reviewer interaction dynamics, and reviewer disagreement patterns. Our results show that factors beyond scientific novelty significantly shape acceptance outcomes. In particular, the rebuttal stage emerges as a decisive phase: timely, substantive author--reviewer communication strongly increases acceptance likelihood, often outweighing initial reviewer skepticism. Clearer writing, earlier submission, and effective disagreement resolution also correlate with higher acceptance probabilities. Based on these findings, we propose data-driven guidelines for authors, reviewers, and meta-reviewers to enhance transparency and fairness in peer review.
filter_reasoning: The paper performs a process-centric analysis of academic peer review to propose guidelines for fairness and transparency, central topics in AI ethics.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: InFi-Check: Interpretable and Fine-Grained Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often hallucinate, yet most existing fact-checking methods treat factuality evaluation as a binary classification problem, offering limited interpretability and failing to capture fine-grained error types. In this paper, we introduce InFi-Check, a framework for interpretable and fine-grained fact-checking of LLM outputs. Specifically, we first propose a controlled data synthesis pipeline that generates high-quality data featuring explicit evidence, fine-grained error type labels, justifications, and corrections. Based on this, we construct large-scale training data and a manually verified benchmark InFi-Check-FG for fine-grained fact-checking of LLM outputs. Building on these high-quality training data, we further propose InFi-Checker, which can jointly provide supporting evidence, classify fine-grained error types, and produce justifications along with corrections. Experiments show that InFi-Checker achieves state-of-the-art performance on InFi-Check-FG and strong generalization across various downstream tasks, significantly improving the utility and trustworthiness of factuality evaluation.
filter_reasoning: The paper develops methods to increase the trustworthiness and factuality of LLMs, which is directly related to AI safety and reliability.

venue_name: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
title: Stable Reasoning, Unstable Responses: Mitigating LLM Deception via Stability Asymmetry
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) expand in capability and application scope, their trustworthiness becomes critical. A vital risk is intrinsic deception, wherein models strategically mislead users to achieve their own objectives.
